acceptance.duplicate_gate: Versioned domain-tagged semantic-core key derived before writes; best-effort repository search and exact public Slack recovery-token search must return zero matches. Duplicate means no event, no CURRENT update, and no Slack.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Commit and read back this immutable event; fetch CURRENT again; update only if version=42, projection digest=1c79471da8cff1bff2b651b248f900f80b5083a2206fd95eff7e8815f1f10e9b, and blob=fbddeb15f18c9842524c7f13ab3e9ea143838c94; then read back CURRENT, this event, and predecessor.
acceptance.slack_rule: Perform no Slack write before Git v43 is durable. After final Git readback, reconstruct exactly one sanitized recovery pointer from the immutable event plus CURRENT, carrying both the event digest and idempotency key as independent lookup anchors. Do not rewrite CURRENT merely to embed the Slack link.
acceptance.stale_rule: Any wake not observing exact v42, prior digest 862248bf..., projection digest 1c79471d..., and blob fbddeb15... must not advance.

experiment.controlled_factor: Keep event canonicalization, v3 semantic-core idempotency, event-first write/readback, exact second CURRENT read, and single-file blob-SHA guard fixed; vary only the recovery-pointer reconstruction contract from one exact token to dual lookup anchors: recovery token plus event digest/idempotency key.
experiment.hypothesis: After a confirmed prewrite Slack absence, the Git-backed object can advance independently and one post-readback Slack recovery pointer can be reconstructed with two immutable lookup anchors without rewriting object state.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: The proposed idempotency key or recovery token already exists; CURRENT is not exact v42 on the second read; event digest recomputation fails; final chain bindings disagree; Slack is posted before Git v43 readback; the posted pointer omits either immutable lookup anchor; or more than one recovery pointer is emitted.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is a controlled same-run omission and reconstruction, not a real Slack outage, process crash, delayed replay, distinct-carrier recovery, or server-enforced uniqueness test. Dual lookup anchors improve auditability but do not create atomicity or uniqueness. Slack search can lag or omit messages. Git event creation, CURRENT replacement, validation reads, Slack search, and Slack posting are separate effects. Git provides no cross-file atomicity, database isolation, linearizability, exactly-once execution, referential integrity, server-side idempotency uniqueness, Slack atomicity, lock fairness, or automatic orphan repair.
canonical_transition.rollback: Append a compensating event from the then-current version; never delete this event or Slack recovery message; replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
canonical_transition.transaction_time_evidence: AUTOMATION_RUNTIME_CLOCK+NATIVE_TASK_INVENTORY_READBACK+GITHUB_COMMIT_METADATA; Slack search/post and Git writes are not one transaction boundary
